key_insight: Healthy-looking projector outputs can hide collapsed encoder representations in Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs). Batch normalization removes a component shared across inputs, leaving downstream regularization unable to correct it as meaningful differences between representations shrink.
problem_solved: Preventing hidden representation collapse that projector-level constraints alone fail to detect or stop.
method: Analyze encoder representations as a shared component plus input-specific differences.
Identify how batch normalization masks the shared component, creating a blind spot for post-projector regularization.
Introduce SADL (Supply And Demand Loss) to address collapse; the provided abstract is truncated before explaining its formulation.
impact: For practitioners training JEPAs, well-constrained projector outputs are not enough to establish representation quality. Monitoring encoder-level diversity can help reveal collapse that downstream checks miss.
visual_elements: Encoder → batch-normalized projector pipeline highlighting where the shared component disappears.
Vector diagram separating a shared representation component from input-specific differences.
Before-and-after embedding plots illustrating distinct inputs converging toward collapse.
Blind-spot illustration contrasting encoder collapse with apparently well-behaved projector outputs.
paper_title: SADL: On the Demand-Supply Geometry of Representation Collapse
paper_authors: Junhan Sun, Yigui Feng, Mingzhe Liu, Haoyan Xu, Lei Ye
